record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Determine all pairs of spherical (d−1)-polytopes K1 and K2 for which there exists a chiral d-polytope whose facets are isomorphic to K1 and whose vertex-figures are isomorphic to K2.

evidence.quote: Problem 17 Determine all spherical (d−1)-polytopes K1 and K2 for which there exists a chiral d-polytope with facets isomorphic to K1 and vertex-figures isomorphic to K2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract d-polytope is a partially ordered set P with a strictly monotone rank function onto {-1,0,1,...,d} such that: (i) P has a unique minimum element (of rank -1) and a unique maximum element (of rank d); (ii) every maximal chain (flag) of P has exactly d+2 elements; (iii) P is strongly flag-connected; and (iv) P satisfies the diamond condition, i.e., whenever F < G with rank(G) - rank(F) = 2, there are exactly two elements H with F < H < G. Elements of rank j are called j-faces; the (d-1)-faces are the facets, and for a vertex v (a 0-face), the vertex-figure at v is the section consisting of all faces strictly between v and the maximum element. An automorphism of P is a rank-preserving bijection that respects the order. P is said to be chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags such that any two adjacent flags lie in different orbits. An abstract polytope is called spherical if it is isomorphic to the face lattice of a convex polytope (equivalently, its order complex is a sphere of the appropriate dimension).

Determine all pairs (K_1, K_2) of spherical abstract (d-1)-polytopes such that there exists a chiral abstract d-polytope all of whose facets are isomorphic to K_1 and all of whose vertex-figures are isomorphic to K_2.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of classifying which pairs of spherical (d-1)-polytopes can serve as facets and vertex-figures of a chiral d-polytope is listed among open problems on chiral polytopes. Recent work (e.g., constructions of chiral polytopes of large rank, chiral extensions, and Schläfli-symbol restrictions) provides partial results — chiral d-polytopes with prescribed regular facets exist in some cases for small d, but no complete classification of admissible (K_1, K_2) pairs is known. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems (Appendix C) - Abstract Chiral Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Appendix listing open problems on abstract chiral polytopes, including classification questions for facet/vertex-figure types.
status_evidence.claim: The classification question is included in a contemporary list of open problems on chiral polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Construction of chiral polytopes of large rank with alternating groups
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of chiral polytopes of arbitrarily large rank, addressing existence questions but not full classification.
status_evidence.claim: Recent constructions provide existence results for chiral polytopes but do not yield a complete classification of facet/vertex-figure pairs.

status_evidence.title: On the Schläfli symbol of chiral extensions of polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the possible Schläfli symbols of chiral extensions of polytopes, giving partial information on facet types.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on Schläfli symbols of chiral polytopes exist but the general classification remains incomplete.
